newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on exports, talk of India buy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on exports, talk of India buy.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures ended the session higher on solid weekly export sales data and talk that India would tender for wheat over the weekend, traders and analysts said.
"Wheat, I really think, is being supported by the export sales," said Jack Scoville analyst with LIT America. "They (sales) continue to run at a pretty good clip."

On Thursday, before the market's open, the U.S. Department of Agriculture reported net weekly export sales of 497,000 tonnes. Those sales came in well above trade expectations for 100,000 to 300,000 tonnes.

Many in the trade were also anticipating India to tender for 500,000 tonnes of wheat over the weekend. This on the heels of reports from U.S. and European exporters and traders that India recently bought one million tonnes of Australian wheat. However, the Australian Wheat Board would not confirm the sale.
Some of Thursday's gains were also linked to short covering before USDA's 1997 planted acreage and quarterly grain stocks report on Monday, CBOT traders said.
CBOT wheat futures closed up six to eight cents per bushel with May up 6-1/4 at $4.01-3/4 and July up eight at $3.98-1/2.
Analysts expect the USDA report to show wheat plantings dropping sharply to 70.10 million acres from 75.64 million last year.
Expectations that recent wet weather in the Midwest will promote disease in the soft red winter wheat crop also contributed to the market's strength, Scoville said.
On the day, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought two million bushels May and two million bushels July. Tenco bought one million December and July and two million May.
Refco sold five million bushels July and two million May, pit sources said.
In options trading, FIMAT Futures, Inc. bought 300 July $4.10 puts and sold 200 July $4.00 puts.
The CBOT estimated Thursday's wheat volume at 20,000 contracts, up from Wednesday's actual volume of 17,098 contracts, according to CBOT data.
